title: Metal cutting head producing sparks over slatted support bed
objects_and_counts: No people are visible in the photographed scene.
One cutting head or nozzle assembly is visible near the top-centre of the image; the nozzle is engaged in a cut and emitting sparks.
Multiple metal workpiece fragments are visible on the support bed immediately under the cutting head; at least three distinct flat metal pieces can be individually seen in the immediate cutting area.
One cylindrical metal tool or component lies on the support bed in the lower-right foreground; it is partially cropped by the frame on its right side.

The support bed consists of a dense array of short vertical slats or pins (a slatted or pin-type bed) occupying the central and background image regions; individual pins are numerous and not counted exactly.
Numerous bright orange sparks are visible radiating from the cutting point; these are transient particles in the scene rather than separate fixed objects.
spatial_relations: The cutting head/nozzle assembly is located near the top-centre of the image and projects downward toward the support bed.
The active cutting point is located slightly below and to the right of the cutting head centre, with sparks radiating outward from that point across the bed.
Flat metal workpiece fragments lie directly underneath and slightly forward of the cutting point on the slatted/pin bed.
A cylindrical metal object lies in the lower-right foreground on top of the support bed and is closer to the viewer than the cutting point and workpieces.
The slatted or pin-type support bed fills the central portion of the image and extends into the background behind the cutting head.
colours_and_materials: The machine cutting head and surrounding hardware appear metallic silver/grey.
The support bed and many components appear dark grey to bluish-grey; fine debris on the bed gives a textured, granular appearance.
Sparks from the cut are bright orange-yellow and create high-contrast streaks against the darker bed.
The visible metal workpieces under the nozzle appear silver to grey, consistent with bare metal.
